analysis: The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (date bump, new selected-model recovery paragraphs at head lines 371-408) and docs/architecture/model-autopilot.md (date bump, adoption-ends row, new recovery and placement-release prose, invariant 10, restart failure mode). No source, protocol, key-handling, attestation or encryption code is touched, so there is no direct regression to A-001, A-003, A-015/A-016, TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. I read the described behaviors as a design claim and did not verify them against code. The recovery loop, which is capacity-tick driven with allowEviction:false, can unload idle resident models, release Autopilot adoptions after hold expiry, and withdraw a released model so it refuses requests as model_not_selected. Its stated protections are never evicting the ordinary selection, pins, held or busy slots, or advertised models a request could reload. That mainly affects availability and placement (T-029-like), not confidentiality. The docs cite ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift, ProviderLoop+SelectedModelPlacementPolicy.swift, isProtectedFromRecoveryEviction, selectedModelRecoveryVictimWait and adoptionReleaseTime. None of these were supplied, and the docs say the placement policy is pending owner review. A later integration pass should check that the implementation matches: the protection predicates, in-flight request completion on release, and no bypass of the load gate, pending-load claims or the post-load KV headroom check. A consumer or coordinator influencing eviction via cold-route timing is a plausible but unverified availability concern. The edited docs do not change the T-041 prefix-cache posture, which stays unchanged. No threat-model update is warranted from the docs alone, since they make no new security or attestation claims.
